subject: Urgent: BlueOak — sudden latency and hallucination surge after v2.1 (quant) rollout
messages:
From: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@blueoak.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production regression since v2.1 (q8_eco) deploy — immediate impact

Grace / Redwood team,

We started seeing a notable jump in latency and an increase in incorrect outputs (hallucinations / unexpected completions) starting ~08:30 PST this morning right after our scheduled model switch to v2.1 with the q8_eco quant profile. P95 for text-generation requests jumped from ~210ms to ~620ms and the error rate (misleading or off-topic completions) is up ~6x for our checkout assistant flows. This is causing user-visible failures on our site.

We need an immediate rollback to the previous serving variant (v2.0-quant-stable) or routing to a known-good path. This is a live revenue-impacting regression and we are within 48 hours of a major marketing push; SLA credits and escalation will be requested if this continues.

Attached: screenshots of error outputs and a short log snippet.

Please advise ETA for mitigation.

—
Aditi Shah
Head of Platform Reliability
BlueOak Commerce

Grace

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Production regression since v2.1 (q8_eco) deploy — immediate impact

Grace / team —

I’ve pulled traces for BlueOak for the 08:15–09:00 window. High-level observations:

- There is a sustained spike in decode time starting at ~08:29 PST that correlates with the rollout of v2.1/q8_eco.
- Batch sizes for BlueOak’s high-concurrency tail increased due to a tenant autoscaling-induced burst; combined with kernel fallback, p95 climbed rapidly.
- We see a handful of completions where token alignment looks off (gaps in prompt+response), which could explain the hallucinations Aditi saw.

Attachments: latency_report_q8_vs_stable.csv, trace_snippet.txt.

Immediate ask to engineering (Soojin): can we flip routing for BlueOak to v2.0-quant-stable and/or push a temporary config that disables continuous batching for this tenant? We should also consider a short tokenization sanity-check step for high-value flows.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency_report_q8_vs_stable.csv (csv); trace_snippet.txt (txt)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Exec visibility — BlueOak live-sla risk and rollback approval needed

Team —

Looping in Karthik for risk / product oversight. This is escalating toward an SLA breach (BlueOak is threatening credits if unresolved). A brief on impact:

- P95 latency moved 3x; error/quality regression on critical checkout flows.
- BlueOak is a strategic mid-market customer (deal BO-4321). We have 2 renewal milestones coming and this is high-visibility.

Decision request: approve immediate tenant routing rollback to v2.0-quant-stable and apply temporary config: disable continuous batching for BlueOak + cap batch-size to 4 for the next 6 hours. Engineering will monitor; if stable we keep that routing and schedule a formal postmortem.

I’m recommending we offer a 10% service credit for the affected window if rollback is not full mitigation within 6 hours. Please respond with thumbs-up/thumbs-down.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer & Product Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rollback_playbook.pdf (pdf)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Root cause and mitigation plan for BlueOak regression

Team —

Summary of findings from initial investigation:

- Root cause: the q8_eco quant profile triggers a code path that falls back from the fused multi-head attention kernel to a slower reference kernel on our current GPU compilation when sequence lengths exceed 512 in streaming flows. That fallback increases per-token decode time and amplifies tail latency during bursts.
- Secondary effect: tokenization normalization differences between v2.0 and v2.1 lead to occasional token boundary drift, which on a small fraction of requests produced off-topic tokens (observed as hallucinations).

Proposed immediate mitigations (ordered):
1) Route all BlueOak production traffic to v2.0-quant-stable (already staged in canary).
2) Disable continuous batching for tenant ID BO-4321 and set max batch size to 4.
3) Enable an on-request tokenization sanity check for checkout prompts (cheap guard).
4) Run an accelerated rollback validation for other tenants that use q8_eco to confirm no broader impact.

I can execute steps 1–2 within 20 minutes pending rollback authorization from ops. If we get authorization, we will monitor p50/p95 and error rate; target is to restore p95 to <=300ms within 2 hours.

Soojin Lee
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Update: BlueOak rollback complete and next steps

Aditi —

Quick update and apology for the disruption. We completed the routing rollback to v2.0-quant-stable at 15:42 PST on 3 Mar. Initial monitoring shows p95 back down to ~240ms and a large reduction in off-topic completions on the checkout flows.

Steps we’ve taken:
- Rolled BlueOak to v2.0-quant-stable (fully live at 15:42 PST).
- Disabled continuous batching for BO-4321 and capped batch size to 4.
- Collected traces and example failure cases for the postmortem.

Next steps for Redwood:
- Scheduled postmortem with BlueOak on Thu 4 Mar, 10:00 PST to walk through root cause and long-term mitigation.
- Engineering will run a broader rollout audit for q8_eco across high-traffic tenants this week and delay further rollout until we have a fix or a safer kernel fallback.
- We will issue a goodwill credit (10%) for the affected window and include a formal incident report after the postmortem.

Again, sincerely sorry for the disruption — we’ll be working to ensure this does not recur. Please reply with any immediate questions or additional evidence you’d like us to include in the postmortem.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Account Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
